provider: EuroHPC JU Regular Access (LUMI, Leonardo, MareNostrum 5, JUPITER)

free_tier.stated: LUMI-O object storage: 150 TB default quota per project, expandable up to 2.1 PB, retained for the project lifetime, billing rate 0.25x.
free_tier.notes: Access to EuroHPC systems is free of charge.

retention.stated: LUMI-O object storage is retained for the project lifetime.

egress.terms: Free for allocation holders within the facility; object storage endpoints (LUMI-O S3) are internet-reachable.

tooling: LUMI-O is S3-compatible (rclone 's3'); other sites expose Lustre/POSIX plus Globus.
chaining: Storage comes attached to a compute award, so a storage-heavy proposal can be packaged inside a modest compute request. One-year allocations with successive cut-offs allow re-application.

limits.value: allocations are granted for one (1) year

limits_note: Geography is the hard gate: eligibility is limited to entities 'established or located in an EU Member State or in a Participating State or in a third country associated to the Digital Europe Programme or to Horizon Europe'. The published country list runs to ~45 states (incl. Turkiye, Tunisia, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Israel, UK) and excludes everyone else. Allocations are one year; ~4 months from cut-off to access.

identity_cost.detail: Applicants must be researchers from academia, research institutes, public authorities or industry established or located in an EU Member State, a Participating State or a third country associated to the Digital Europe Programme or to Horizon Europe.

reliability_note: Well-run; the constraint is purely eligibility and the compute-justification burden.
confidence_note: Documented from vendor pages re-read on 2026-11-04: https://docs.lumi-supercomputer.eu/storage/ (LUMI-O 150 TB, project lifetime), https://www.eurohpc-ju.europa.eu/supercomputers/supercomputers-access-policy-and-faq_en (free of charge; eligibility) and https://www.eurohpc-ju.europa.eu/eurohpc-ju-call-proposals-regular-access-mode_en (one-year allocations).
